title: Jenner's experiment: sequencing cards
subject: History
source: Written for history/y4 lesson 9 (Jenner's experiment sequencing cards (portal printable))
intro: Lesson 9. Cut out the cards and put them in order. Then write one sentence on why the experiment mattered.

cards: Jenner noticed that milkmaids who caught cowpox did not seem to catch smallpox.
In 1796 Jenner took material from a cowpox sore.
He put it into a small cut on a boy's arm.
The boy became slightly ill with cowpox, then recovered.
Later, Jenner exposed the boy to smallpox. He did not catch it.
Jenner tested more people and published his results in 1798.
Vaccination spread; smallpox was declared wiped out in 1980.
blocks.task: put them in the order they happened.
blocks.answer: In the order printed: noticing milkmaids; 1796 cowpox material; into a cut; mild illness; exposed to smallpox, no illness; more tests and published 1798; smallpox declared eradicated in 1980.

questions.q: Why was Jenner's experiment so important?
questions.a: It led to vaccination, which protected millions of people and wiped out smallpox.
